saveSpec.exe: Cyberpunk2077.exe product version 2.5, file version 3.0.5813403, 66,704,848 bytes
saveSpec.note: Complete record of the Cyberpunk 2077 save format as understood by the RelicWriter project: container, versions, reusable types, shared formats, and the layout and availability of every node name seen. Status values: verified (the layout consumed every byte of every instance in the local saves), partial (some bytes undecoded), untested (read from the game or reference tools, no local save exercises it), open (unknown). Layouts of nodes whose names also appear in other versions carry version gates (when="v >= N") so one entry covers all versions.

conventions.rule: All integers are little-endian. Node layouts exclude the leading u32 node id; the layout of a node is the bytes after the id up to the first child (<fields>), and the bytes after the last child (<trailing>).
when="..." is a condition over v (save version, header offset 4), a (archive version) and earlier fields of the same node by name. Absent means always. Operators: >=, >, <=, <, ==, !=, and, or.

Field elements: u8 u16 u32 u64 i32 f32 (fixed size); cname (u64 hash from v >= 193, string below); string (varint-length ASCII); name (a string used as a name); tweakDBID (8 bytes); bytes size="N"; blob (u32 size then bytes); varint.

array: count is the count type (u8 u16 u32 varint or a literal number) or countField names an earlier field; elementType names a primitive or a <type>; elementBytes is the size of an opaque element; a nested <element> describes a struct element.

parallelArrays: one count, then each column in turn. countedArrays: all varint counts first, then each array. repeat: repeat the children countField times, or once per element of the array named by over. group: fields that appear together (usually under a when). switch/case/default: choose on a field value. repeatToEnd: repeat until the data is used up. optionalTail: bytes present only when they fit. undecoded: bytes whose layout is unknown. computed: a value derived from other fields. child: where a child node sits among the node's own data. ref: a reusable <type>.
source="0x..." gives the address of the game function that reads the structure in the 2.5 exe; addresses move with every build.

container.note: sav.dat. All integers are little-endian. Four-character tags are stored byte-reversed on disk, so VASC on disk is CSAV. The layout is identical in all four verified versions apart from the chunk table capacity. Other versions are untested.

saveFolder.note: %USERPROFILE%\Saved Games\CD Projekt Red\Cyberpunk 2077\<SaveName>\ contains sav.dat, metadata.9.json and screenshot.png. metadata.9.json holds readable summary fields (level, life path, buildPatch, playTime and so on) and is what the load menu reads.
saveFolder.open: The exact schema of metadata.9.json and how it relates to sav.dat.

header.field: The game's gameGameVersion enum, see versions/gameVersions.

Length-prefixed string. CyberCAT treats it as an unused padding byte; CSE and WolvenKit's reader (GameDefPath) read a string. Empty (00) in every save seen, so all readings agree. metadata.9.json has a matching gameDefinition field, also empty. What the game writes when it is not empty is open.

Packed: hour = clock >> 22, minutes = (clock >> 16) & 63, seconds = (clock >> 10) & 63, milliseconds = clock & 1023. WolvenKit reads clock and date as one u64 timestamp with the clock in the low half; the split into two u32 is CyberCAT's.
Packed: year = date >> 20, month = 1 + (date >> 15) % 32, day = 1 + (date >> 10) % 32. Checked on ManualSave-6 (written 2026-10-23 21:22): clock 0x0556b578 is 21:22, date 0x7ea4d800 is 2026-10-23.
195 in all four saves, including patch 1.04. CSE reads it only when saveVersion >= 83 and assumes 192 otherwise. CSE accepts up to 195.
N. A reader must trust only this count, not the table padding.
Zero padding; may hold stale bytes (in at least one save the padding held entries that do not belong to the file).
N LZ4 chunks back to back.
Absolute file offset of the node table.
header.open: Whether the string at offset 12 can ever be non-empty, and what the length prefix looks like for long strings.

chunkTable.note: Chunks are contiguous: each entry's offset + compressedSize equals the next offset and the last one ends exactly at the node table offset. The uncompressed size is 262,144 for every chunk except the last, which holds the remainder.

capacity.layout: A third layout that CyberCAT's original code does not list.
capacity.note: firstChunkOffset = 33 + 12 * entries. CyberCAT finds the capacity as (firstChunkOffset - 33) / 12. CSE writes the table with a minimum firstChunkOffset of 0xC21.
capacity.open: Whether the game picks the layout by save version or by save size.

chunk.bytes: Raw LZ4 block, no frame header.
chunk.note: Concatenating the decompressed chunks gives the node data stream.
chunk.open: Console saves: CSE detects chunks that lack the 4ZLX tag (it calls this "ps4w") and treats them as uncompressed, and also accepts the magic SAVE. Neither is in the PC saves.

logicalOffsets.note: Node offsets live in a logical space: logical = firstChunkOffset + position in the decompressed stream. In all four versions the lowest node offset equals firstChunkOffset and the highest node end equals firstChunkOffset + total decompressed size.

repeat.name: nodes
repeat.i32: Index of the next sibling, -1 for none.
Index of the first child, -1 for none.
repeat.u32: Includes the node's children and any data after them.

nodeTable.u32: Repeat of the offset at end-8.

varintEncoding.note: First byte: bit 7 sign, bit 6 continuation, bits 0-5 value. Each later byte: bits 0-6 value, bit 7 continuation. Value bits are little-endian groups: the first byte holds bits 0-5, the next bits 6-12, and so on. In every save the whole node table is consumed exactly.

stringEncoding.note: A varint length followed by the characters. The length is stored negated (sign bit set), meaning single-byte characters; CyberCAT reads it as -length single-byte characters. Every name and string in the saves is stored this way. A positive length is never seen and CyberCAT does not handle it.
stringEncoding.open: How a positive name length would be encoded.

nodeNames.note: Node names include version suffixes: PersistencySystem in 193 became PersistencySystem2 from 261, and names like ProgressAggregator_v5 carry a schema version. Nodes whose names start with a quote (such as "Core") are child nodes inside other nodes; the quote is part of the name as stored.

tree.rule: Nodes form a tree. childId is the node's first child and nextId is its next sibling; -1 means none. Both are indexes into the node table.
Starting at node 0 and following nextId gives the root nodes (61 to 88 of them, depending on the save). Following childId and nextId reaches every node exactly once.
nextId is always greater than the node's own index, so the table is in depth-first order.
A parent's byte range contains all its children's ranges.
Every node's payload starts with a u32 node id that equals the node's index in the node table.
A parent's payload is not made up only of its children. For example GameSessionDesc (58 bytes) has its first child at +4, so there is data before it.

gaps.note: Bytes between sibling nodes: a node's recorded range does not always end where the next sibling starts. In all four save versions some siblings have a gap of 4 to 16 bytes (for example between UniqueItemCounter and inventory, and between itemData nodes). The gap belongs to no node's size. A writer that wants an identical node table must keep these bytes. The gaps are not decoded, except that for inventory they hold item id headers (see the inventory node).

trailingData.note: A node's own data does not always end where its first child begins. Some nodes write further fields after their last child, inside the same node range. A parser that stops at the first child misses them. Known cases: TimeSystem (17 bytes), GPSSystem (one 12-byte position per child), GameAudio (a string, 261+), ItemDropStorageManager (u32), and inventory (24 or 36 bytes in some 277 saves).

rewriting.note: Rewriting a save: node sizes, offsets, chunk table and trailer all change when a node grows, and the game may check more than these. Writing a save back and loading it in the game has not been tried. RelicWriter.Common reads and writes the container; reading then writing gives the same node tree and a byte-identical node table on all 24 local saves.
CSE re-serialises each node it understands and compares the bytes with the original before allowing edits (test_reserialize in savegame.h); that check should be copied.

observed.note: Missing: every save version between these, and anything from the first release (1.0) up to 1.04. The save version for patches 1.x is probably in the 190s, but only 193 has been seen. Node counts vary with how far into the game the save is, so they are not a version signal.

versions.headerNumbers: Three numbers in the header. CSE names them v1, v2, v3; CyberCAT names them save version, game version and archive version. Save version is what node parsers branch on. Game version is the game's gameGameVersion enum; 8 is CP77_PatchDay0_Hotfix2_V2: early builds used small sequence numbers and patch-based numbering (patch times 1000) starts at 1.1, so a 1.04 save with game version 8 is expected. Archive version is 195 in all four saves; CSE accepts up to 195 and rejects anything higher ("will change soon").

gameVersions.source: gameGameVersion enum in WolvenKit, from the game's reflection data. It stops at 2.3, so 2310 (our 269 save) and 2500 (our 277 save) come from our saves and the buildPatch in their metadata agrees. The 1.4 value (1310) is lower than the 1.3 development build: do not assume game versions only go up with patch number.

version.name: 1.2 hotfixes 1 to 4 (1240 is the first DLC build)

referenceToolGates.note: Version-gated parsing in CyberCAT and CSE, from their source, not from our checks, except the two rows labelled game code which were read from the exe. Nothing newer than CSE v0.6.1 (May 2024, built for patch 2.12) is covered, and its version checks stop at save version 221. The game's own loaders have a threshold at 248 for inventory/itemData that the tools do not; whether it changes bytes in those nodes is open (the tools parse the 261, 269 and 277 saves without it).

Reads the old `PersistencySystem` node (with `PSData` children). From 205 it reads `TypeDatabase_v2` and `PersistencySystem2` instead. **From the game's own code** (patch 2.5 exe), checked against our four saves: 193 has the old node, 261 and later the new one.
The node starts with the id array described in [save-node-formats.md](save-node-formats.md).

loaderThresholds.note: Produced from the exe: for each node name the exe holds a small function that returns the name hash; the functions that call it are the node loader and saver. 65 of them compare the stream's save version with constants. Each constant is "the layout changes at save version >= N" (a test K < version becomes N = K + 1). Checked against the reference tools (item loaders 96, 189, 220 = tools' 97, 190, 221; appearance 168 as in CSE; StatsSystem 276 sits between our 269 and 277 saves). Limits: read from decompiled code with a pattern match; a row with several nodes does not say which node a threshold belongs to; small values (below about 30) and PersistencySystem thresholds other than 125 and 205 may come from a reused variable. What each change is, is not known unless described in a node entry. The highest threshold is 277 (PhoneManager), so 277 is the newest save version this build has a layout for. Known meanings: StatsSystem 276 is the shared-buffer layout; PersistencySystem 205 is the switch to TypeDatabase_v2 and PersistencySystem2, 125 is whether the id array exists; inventory and itemData 97, 190, 221 are the item id fields, 248 is not in the tools; CharacetrCustomization_Appearances 168 is the tag field.

referenceToolSupport.note: CyberCAT-SimpleGUI README lists patch 1.5X and 1.23 as fully supported and 1.3 as partial, but is out of date. Its current code loads saves through WolvenKit's CyberpunkSaveReader, which refuses any save with a game version below 2000 (patch 2.0), so it cannot open a 193 save. The CyberCAT.Core.dll it still ships has exactly the same parser set as the archived WolvenKit/CyberCAT source.
WolvenKit's reader has one game-version gate: from game version 2110 (patch 2.1 hotfix 1) a node ContainerManager_InjectedLoot carries one more byte per sub-entry.

WolvenKit/CyberCAT was archived with its last change in Feb 2022 (predates Phantom Liberty and 2.x). CSE is the most recent readable source (up to patch 2.12, May 2024). None of the three covers 2.3 or later; the local saves are the only evidence for 269 and 277.

versions.open: Which save versions exist between and before the four observed ones and what each changed. How the game's loader treats older versions (does it upgrade nodes on load, which suffixes does it accept). Whether any save version changes the container layout itself (all four seen share it except the chunk table capacity).

types.note: Reusable structures referenced from node layouts with <ref type="..."/>. A ref with count/countField repeats the type. Conditions use the same variables as in nodes.

type.name: TweakDBID
type.u32: CRC-32 of the record name (for example Items.money).
type.note: Verified by finding Items.money in the inventory of every save version. Turning an id back into a name needs a list of known record names, which a save does not contain.

type.name: CName
type.note: In a node: a u64 from save version 193 up, a string below (the loader tests for 193 exactly). The u64 is (length << 32) | FNV-1a-32 of the name. In system blobs a CName is a u16 index into the string pool. In property streams a CName is a u64 hash.

type.name: FNV1a64
type.note: Start at 0xcbf29ce484222325; for each byte xor it in and multiply by 0x100000001b3 modulo 2^64. Used for node names in the game's loaders, property and type names in property streams and TypeDatabase_v2, class names, and gamedataStatType values in the stats shared buffer.

type.name: ItemID
type.tweakDBID: The item record, such as Items.money.
type.u32: 2 on the first item of every save looked at. Exact meaning open.
type.note: The record is 15 bytes in the 193 save and 16 bytes in 261, 269 and 277. Verified at 193 and 261; the thresholds 97, 190 and 221 come from CSE (the game's loaders agree: 96, 189, 220 with the direction of the test applied) and are not tested at the boundaries.

type.name: ItemMod
type.note: A recursive record for an item and the mods attached to it.

group.name: trailer
group.note: Matches the layout of the mod root header. Always present at 193 and above in the saves; below 192 untested.

format.name: systemBlob
format.note: Many nodes store their data as a "system blob": a small serialised object graph that names its own classes and fields (StatsSystem, StatPoolsSystem, ScriptableSystemsContainer, ...). Verified by a throwaway parser written from CSE's source on one save of each version: in every node where the container applies, all objects and all fields were consumed exactly (about 3,900 objects and 13,700 fields). Decoded values match the save's metadata.9.json. Because each object lists its own field names and type names, the structure can be read without the game's class definitions; what cannot be read without them is which two-byte values are enums and which are empty structs.

usedBy.status: detected by checking that the node's data has the header with a size that fits exactly

node.name: StreamingPrefetchParamsNew
node.note: Seen only in one of the three 263 saves (ManualSave-4); layout not read.

node.name: scanningController
node.note: In 261 to 277 it does not have this layout.

node.name: questSceneDataHelper
node.note: Does not fit: different layout in the versions that have it (header fields are inconsistent). Not decoded.

usedBy.note: The list is what matched in the four saves. Other nodes may use the format and just did not match, or the node may be absent from the sample.

blob.u32: Equals the node's own data length minus 8.
Also the size of the string descriptor table.
blob.array: The count repeats the header's. In ScriptableSystemsContainer the root names are 64-bit hashes, one per sub-system (16 to 20); the hash function is open.

A blob can have more data after the main blob. The blob size field does not cover it; the node's data ends exactly after it. PSData has it (8,615 hashes in the 193 save). Verified in the 193 PSData; not checked in the other blob nodes.
blob.rule: Offsets inside the blob are relative to base, the position right after the header (and after the root name list, if present).
string data offset <= object descriptors offset <= object data offset.

stringPool.rule: Starts at base. The first stringDataOffset bytes are descriptors, 4 bytes each, so the number of strings is that offset divided by 4.
Each descriptor is a u32: the low 24 bits are the string's offset from base, the high 8 bits are its length including a terminating zero byte.
The strings follow the descriptors and are zero-terminated. Every string ended in a zero byte and every index was in range.
The pool holds class names, field names, type names and also enum values and name (CName) values, so each distinct string appears once.

objectDescriptor.u32: A class name from the string pool.
Relative to base; increases from one object to the next; the first equals the object data offset. An object's data ends where the next one's begins; the last one ends at the end of the blob.

element.u32: Relative to the start of the object.

object.rule: The first field's offset equals 2 + 8 * count, offsets increase, and each field runs up to the next field's offset (the last to the end of the object).

An empty object, or a struct with no fields, is just 00 00. Fields that hold the type's default value appear to be left out: array elements often list fewer fields than their class has (for example a skill entry with only currentLevel). Inferred from what was seen and from a comment in CSE.

enumProblem.status: resolved for 2.31 and earlier; types added in 2.5 are not covered
enumProblem.note: An enum value takes two bytes, and so does an empty struct (00 00); the bytes and the type name do not say which. The game's type data does: a type is an enum if it is in the enum list (cp2077-nativedb enums.json, 1,524 enums). Of 27 names a first parser took for enums, 19 were enums and 8 were structs (gameStatPoolModifier, gameSEquipSlot, UIScriptableSystemAttributeLevel, gameGodModeData, STrait, SAttributeData, SNewPerk, RecipientData). A reader needs that enum list, and it must match the save's game version.

format.open: Handle semantics: the root versus handle object split, and what the handle target classes are. The root name hash function. Default values per class (needed to write blobs back). questSceneDataHelper and scanningController (from 261 on), which do not match this layout. Whether other nodes in unseen saves use it.

format.name: propertyStream
format.note: Some nodes store an object as a list of its properties, each carrying the hash of its name and the hash of its type, so a reader can find the property in a class and skip what it does not know. Read from the game's serialiser (FUN_140279248 writes, FUN_1403ea008 reads) with Ghidra and tested on the saves. Verified on 261, 269 and 277: all entries of PersistencySystem2 (88,050, 90,985 and 57,948) parse and consume every byte. Property and type names come from the 2.31 type dump. The 193 save has no PersistencySystem2 (its PSData uses the system blob format).

propertyList.u64: FNV-1a 64-bit hash of the property name (for example isInitialized). 0 ends a nested list.
FNV-1a 64-bit hash of the property's type name as the game spells it (Bool, TweakDBID, array:Int32, handle:DeviceOperationsContainer, EDeviceStatus, a class name).

format.rule: Only properties that differ from their default are written; the writer skips equal ones and drops a nested object entirely if nothing in it is written. A missing property means default, and the default has to come from the game's class definition, which the save does not contain.

The top-level list of an entry has no terminator of its own; it ends where the entry's data ends. Entries often end with some u64 zeros (0 to 506 seen, mostly 0 or 1). They are only ever at the end. Why the number varies is open; the likeliest cause is how nested lists in arrays are closed.

value.type: Int64, Uint64, CName, TweakDBID, CRUID, NodeRef
value.encoding: 8 bytes. CName and NodeRef are hashes (a name or path is not stored).
The enum's size in bytes, raw value (not a name). 4 for nearly all enums, 1 for vehicleCameraPerspective. The sizes are in the save's TypeDatabase_v2 (table A, kind 0x50).
u32 count, then count elements. Primitives and enums are packed back to back; a struct element is a nested property list ending in a u64 zero.
The same as array:T. Only 4 such types occurred in the sample, so this is lightly tested.
u64: the FNV hash of the actual class of the object (it can be a subclass of T), then a nested property list ending in a u64 zero. A null handle is not written.
A nested property list ending in a u64 zero.

format.rule: What decides how to read a type is its kind in the game's type data: primitive, enum, struct or class, array, handle.
format.untested: Anything older than the 261 save, and any entry class the three saves do not contain. Arrays whose elements are handles, arrays of arrays and the fixed array types. Writing: nothing was written back and loaded into the game.

format.name: statsSharedBuffer
format.note: The 2.5 StatsSystem sharedDataBuffer. The 32,768-byte buffer holds 8,612 bytes of data and is zero-padded after that. The records below consume bytes 0 to 8,612 exactly (190 records), the rest is all zeros, and all 30 slice offsets fall on record boundaries.

slices.note: sharedBufferSlices entries are {offset u32, combined u32}. combined & 0x3FFFFFFF is the slice's size in bytes; bit 30 is set on some slices (meaning unknown). Slices are contiguous: each offset is the previous offset plus its size, and the last ends at 8,612. A slice is a run of whole records.

record.string: Varint length, then characters, as for node names.

format.rule: stat is the FNV-1a 64-bit hash of the gamedataStatType value name (for example LootLevel). All 190 records' stat hashes resolved to a name in the 2.31 enum list.
modifierType is the gameStatModifierType enum index: Additive 0, AdditiveMultiplier 1, Multiplier 2.
Counts in the sample: 170 constant, 14 curve, 6 combined. Curve records name a game curve table (quality_curves, random_distributions) and a column in it.

The combined layout is taken from the old deprecated data class's field order and gives plausible values (LootLevel, AdditiveMultiplier, ref stat NPCWeaponDropRandomizer, 1.0); the whole buffer parses with it.
format.open: The order of the two u32 in the combined record: read as operation = 0 (Addition) and refObject = 2 (Root), but the in-memory class puts refObject (0x4C) before operation (0x50), which would read as refObject = Self and operation = Multiplication. All 6 records have the same pair, so the data cannot tell them apart. Whether other record classes exist, and the meaning of slice bit 30, need more 2.5 saves or the game code.

rtti.note: The game's own list of classes and enums gives what the save files alone cannot: which types are enums, which fields a class has, and which of those the game saves. Source: cp2077-nativedb (MIT), a dump of the game's runtime type information made by RED4.RTTIDumper; cp2077_dump_json.zip and enums.json. Game version of the dump: 2.31 (its gameGameVersion enum ends with CP77_Patch_2_3_Hotfix1 = 2310 and Current = 2310). 15,832 classes and 1,524 enums. The dump stores no default values and no save-format information.

check.result: 8,212 of 8,212 matched in every version, no mismatch

check.name: field name exists on the class in the dump
classes missing from the dump
check.result: gameCurveStatModifierData and gameConstantStatModifierData (only in the 193 save, renamed ..._Deprecated later); CyberwareCustomizationSystem (277 save)

rtti.note: The 6 unknown fields are DataTrackingSystem.achievementsMask in the 193 save (gone by 2.31) and the five new StatsSystem fields in the 277 save. gameSavedStatsDataOptimized and gameBufferSlice (277 only) are also not in the dump. For the nodes tested the field layout was stable from 193 through 2.31 apart from renames and removals; the only structural change found in 2.5 is in the stats system.
rtti.savedFieldsRule: A property is saved if bit 28 of its 64-bit flags is set (scripted classes) or bit 14 is set (native save structures such as gameStatPoolsSystemSave). All 123 (class, field) pairs that appeared in the saves satisfy it; of the pairs that never appeared, 180 fail it and 47 pass it (consistent with "fields holding their default value are left out"). Derived from the 269 save's classes; not confirmed on other game versions' flags.
rtti.limits: The 2.5 changes (StatsSystem classes, CyberwareCustomizationSystem and anything added after 2.31); default values; native node formats (the dump describes classes inside system blobs, not hand-written binary such as inventory or PersistencySystem2); save version history.

ghidra.tool: Ghidra 12.2 headless, demangler, address-table, switch and a few other analyzers off (a first run with everything on ran out of memory at a 12 GB heap)
ghidra.method: Each class has a registration function that sets its name and a second function that registers its properties, one call per field with the field name, the offset in the in-memory object and a type getter. Class-name and field-name strings are found by searching the exe and following their cross-references. Offsets are in-memory offsets, so they give field order and size but not the save layout.

All 138 node names were found as plain strings in the exe. Each has a small getter function (about 71 bytes) that returns its name hash, and the functions that call the getter are that node's loader and saver (203 distinct functions across the 138 names, some shared by several nodes). 65 of them compare the save version with constants.

Node names are looked up through functions returning the FNV-1a-64 hash of the name. The persistency loader tests the save version against 0xCD (205): below it the old PersistencySystem node is read, from 205 TypeDatabase_v2 and PersistencySystem2; in the old path a check at 0x7C (124) decides whether the id array is present.

Stream primitives (vtable calls on the stream object): +0x10 is a raw read or write of size bytes, +0x48 returns the save version, +0x90 means "node exists". FUN_140740168(S,N) means v >= N. Helpers: FUN_1403eaa6c is u32, FUN_1403eaa7c is a CName (u64 if v >= 193), FUN_14027a7c4 is a name (varint string, or a u16 index when the stream has a name table), FUN_14027cab4 is a string, FUN_142f60040 is a varint count.
ghidra.pitfall: Tail-called helpers can lose their arguments in decompiled text (calls like FUN_14073d53c(); with empty parens, and RD(ptr) with the size dropped). Re-decompile such functions fresh to see the real arguments and reads.

rtti.open: A 2.5 RTTI dump: either run RED4.RTTIDumper in the game (needs RED4ext installed into the game folder; needs the maintainer's go-ahead; not done) or read the registrations out of the exe with Ghidra one class at a time.

Nodes whose names start with a quote (such as "Core") are child nodes inside other nodes; the quote is part of the stored name. node.rule: The first 127,384 objects belong to the 127,384 root names, one each, in order. Their classes are ...PS persistent-state classes such as gameScanningComponentPS (22,886), gameVisionModeComponentPS (21,623), gameStatsComponentPS (15,403), gameInventoryPS (9,107) and BaseDestructibleControllerPS (5,381). All handle indexes are inside the object list (the largest is the last object).

Every object's field offsets are consistent and every field value parses with the system blob rules. Field type names are the game's (Bool, EDeviceStatus, array:handle:DeviceOperationBase, static:4,vehicleWheelRuntimePSData, Vector3, gameCommunityID and so on).

A type is read as an enum if it is in the 2.31 enum list. Every enum value found is a valid value of its enum in that list. A struct whose only content is empty looks the same as an enum, so this check shows the lists agree, not that no empty struct was taken for an enum.
Arrays of structs: an element's size is not stored; a reader finds an element's end by parsing it (the end of its last field).

node.name: TypeDatabase_v2
node.note: No children; in saves 261, 269 and 277, not in 193. The save carries its own table of types: the loader compares the node's type table hash with the running game's. If they match it reads the persistent objects directly; if not it rebuilds the type table and remaps. The loader only reads this node when the save version is 205 or above. The sizes add up exactly: 24 + 20*A + 8*B + 12*C equals the blob size in 261, 269 and 277 (115,188, 117,448 and 117,612 bytes), so the node has nothing else in it. Names are hashes (FNV-1a 64-bit).

fields.u32: Equals the node's data length minus 8 (counting the node id). The node id is 3 in all three saves.
3 in all three. The loader treats values above 1 as present and handles 2 specially.
fields.u64: Differs in every save (changes with the game's type data).

element.u64: Hash of a type name: a primitive (Bool), an enum, a class or struct, or a composite such as array:ForcedStateData or handle:gameMountEventOptions. 590 of 737 resolve to a name in the 2.31 type dump.
For arrays and handles the hash of the element or target type (123 of the 134 non-zero ones resolve); 0 otherwise.
element.u32: Size in bytes in the bits from 12 up, a kind code in the low 8 bits.

array.name: classes
array.note: Table B: classes. Entries are sorted by type index. The counts of all B entries add up to the number of C entries (8,230 in the 277 save); C is cut into consecutive runs, one per B entry in order, and a class's run holds that class's properties (5,562 of the 8,221 properties in the 277 save's runs for classes known to the dump are properties of that class in the dump; the rest are probably inherited from classes whose list is shared, or not saved by the dump's flags; not checked).

element.u16: Index into table A of the class.
Differs for every class in all three saves, even where nothing seems to change; a checksum is plausible.
The high byte is the number of properties; the low byte is 0, 1 or (once) 2.

array.name: properties
array.note: Table C: properties. The same property name can appear under several classes. Entries are not sorted.

element.u64: FNV-1a 64-bit hash of the property name. 8,222 of 8,230 match a property name in the 2.31 dump.
element.u32: The low 12 bits are the index of the property's type in table A (verified: Bool = index 705 whose entry is Bool, and the same for Uint32, Int32, TweakDBID, CName and an enum). Bits 12 to 19 are always 0. The bits from 20 up are a byte offset (for example 80, 136 and 232 for Bool properties); what it is an offset in was not confirmed.

kindCodes.note: Only the kind and size of the primitives and enums were checked against known values; the rest are from how the entries group by name. For classes the size is probably the object's size in memory (for example 120 for ExplosiveDeviceControllerPS). The 29 enum sizes found by trial in the 277 save all agree.

array.name: controllers
array.note: kind 1 and 2 objects are 8 and 4 bytes when nothing is queued

case.u32: number of queued notifications; in the 261 saves 4 queued notifications follow in a notification-specific layout that is not decoded

array.name: items
array.note: node is read from save version 224 on

array.name: sets
array.note: node is read from save version 224 on

element.u64: CName of the set (0 when unnamed)

fields.u32: trailing u32 of unknown meaning, zero in the saves seen

fields.u64: four 8-byte values that look like f64 coordinates (unconfirmed)
fields.string: e.g. "Runt..." in some saves (second weather name)

node.name: WorldStateSystem
node.note: Own data of the node (before the child nodes). Layout from game code function 1409bcdec. The gate v>=10 is from the loader and is not tested locally.

parallelArrays.name: namedFlags
parallelArrays.note: names, then one byte per name

parallelArrays.name: hashFlags
parallelArrays.note: u64 hashes, then one byte per hash

parallelArrays.name: hashLists
parallelArrays.note: u64 hashes, then for each hash a varint count and that many 16-byte values

parallelArrays.name: hashLists2
parallelArrays.note: same shape as the previous group

sources.source: Header layout and packed date/time, chunk table handling, node table read and write, the two known chunk table layouts, parsers for a handful of nodes.

The GUI. It loads saves through WolvenKit's save reader (below). It still ships the old compiled `CyberCAT.Core.dll`, which we decompiled and found identical in parser set to the archived CyberCAT source.
The most recent readable parser: header, chunk and node handling, version gates per node, tests that re-serialise nodes and compare bytes, and notes on console saves.

The newest readable save parser, and the one SimpleGUI actually uses. Header with the timestamp and game definition path, the node name list, 50 or so node parsers, and the game's `gameGameVersion` enum. **Licence is GPL-3.0, see below.**
Container overview. Matches what we found.
Type definitions from the game's reflection data. Not yet used. Candidate source for node payload formats.
